WBCE020-05.title: Separation Processes
WBCE020-05.priorKnowledge: The course unit assumes some prior knowledge acquired from courses covering basic chemical engineering and thermodynamic principles (Single Phase Reactors and Technical Thermodynamics).

WBIE003-05.title: Calculus 1 (for IEM)
WBIE003-05.priorKnowledge: The course unit assumes only prior knowledge acquired from Mathematics B as taught in pre-university programmes (VWO) on Dutch secondary schools (or equivalent).

WBIE007-05.title: Operations Research
WBIE007-05.priorKnowledge: Students are expected to have prior knowledge of high school algebra and basic mathematical skills, including simple operations with matrices and vectors.

WBIE009-05.title: Linear Algebra (for IEM)
WBIE009-05.priorKnowledge: The course assumes basic mathematical skills (at VWO level) as well as familiarity with complex numbers (Calculus 1 for IEM).

WBIE011-05.title: Mechatronics
WBIE011-05.priorKnowledge: The course unit assumes prior knowledge acquired from Calculus 1 and Calculus 2, Signals and Systems, Control Engineering from the Bachelor IEM programme, or similar courses.

WBIE014-05.title: Production Planning and Quality Control
WBIE014-05.priorKnowledge: Prior knowledge from the course Global Supply Chain (WBIE005-05) is assumed.

WBIE016-05.title: System Dynamics
WBIE016-05.priorKnowledge: Successful completion of Calculus 1 or an equivalent course is highly desirable.

WBIE017-05.title: Calculus 2 (for IEM)
WBIE017-05.priorKnowledge: The course unit assumes prior knowledge acquired from Calculus 1 and Linear Algebra.

WBIE018-05.title: Design and Construction for IEM
WBIE018-05.priorKnowledge:
The course unit assumes prior knowledge acquired from courses like Production Techniques, Materials and Molecules, Mechanics for IEM, and Computer Aided Design & Manufacturing of the Bachelor IEM (PTL track) programme.

This course is part of the BSc Industrial Engineering and Management (IEM) programme, PTL track, but may also be relevant to students from related programmes such as Applied Physics and Biomedical Engineering.

WBIE024-05.title: Mechanics for IEM
WBIE024-05.priorKnowledge: The course unit assumes prior knowledge from Calculus 1, Calculus 2, and Linear Algebra of the BSc Industrial Engineering and Management degree programme.

WBIE025-05.title: Modelling and Analysis of Complex Networks
WBIE025-05.priorKnowledge: The course unit assumes prior knowledge acquired from Calculus 1 and Calculus 2, Linear Algebra, Statistics and Stochastics, and Signals and Systems from the Bachelor IEM programme.

WBIE028-05.title: Product Technology (IEM)
WBIE028-05.priorKnowledge: The course unit assumes prior knowledge acquired from the second year SPE course units.

WBIE029-05.title: Reactor Engineering
WBIE029-05.priorKnowledge: This course prepares for the courses General Process Equipment (WBCE002-05) and Gas-Liquid Mass Transfer (WBIE036-05).

WBIE030-05.title: Signals and Systems
WBIE030-05.priorKnowledge:
The course unit assumes prior knowledge acquired from the following courses of the BSc IEM programme:
* Calculus 1 (for IEM)
* Calculus 2 (for IEM)
* Linear Algebra (for IEM)

WBIE031-05.title: Technical Thermodynamics (IEM)
WBIE031-05.priorKnowledge:
The course unit assumes prior knowledge acquired from Calculus, Linear Algebra, and Programming, Modelling and Simulation from the BSc IEM degree programme.

The course unit is often followed by, or prepares students for the following courses, in which the learning objectives attained are required as prior knowledge: Gas-liquid Mass Transfer and Product Technology (IEM).

WBIE033-05.title: Computer Aided Design and Manufacturing
WBIE033-05.priorKnowledge:
The course unit assumes prior knowledge acquired from preceding courses such as Mechanics for IEM, which are mandatory in the Production Technology and Logistics (PTL) track of Industrial Engineering and Management (IEM) Bachelor. However, the course unit content is structured so that all relevant concepts from these courses are re-introduced where necessary, including a series of lectures to review solid mechanics and materials fundamentals.

The course unit serves as a bridge between the prerequisite courses mentioned above and subsequent courses such as Design and Construction for IEM, while it also prepares students interested in conducting their Bachelor's dissertation research on mechanical design and engineering-related topics.

WBIE034-05.title: Control Engineering
WBIE034-05.priorKnowledge:
The course unit assumes prior knowledge acquired from Calculus, Linear Algebra, and Signals and Systems (BSc Industrial Engineering and Management).

The course unit prepares students for Mechatronics and Dynamics and Vibrations (BSc IEM, 3rd year), and Analysis and Control of Smart Systems (MSc IEM, MSc Mechanical Engineering, and MSc Systems & Control).

WBIE035-05.title: Dynamics of Engineering Systems
WBIE035-05.priorKnowledge: The course serves as the finalization of the mathematics learning path of the Bachelor IEM program and, as such, follows the courses "Calculus 1 (for IEM)," "Calculus 2 (for IEM)" and "Linear Algebra." The course content complements prior courses "Programming, Modeling and Simulation," "System Dynamics," "Materials and Molecules" and "Physical Transport Phenomena". Students are assumed to have prior knowledge from preceding courses, especially on ordinary and partial differential equations, linear algebra and basic modeling and programming skills.

WBIE036-05.title: Gas-Liquid Mass Transfer
WBIE036-05.priorKnowledge: The course unit assumes prior knowledge acquired from the BSc Industrial Engineering Management (SPE) programme. Especially, the successful completion of the course Reactor Engineering WBIE029-05 is assumed when entering this course.

WBIE040-05.title: Production Techniques
WBIE040-05.priorKnowledge:
The course unit assumes prior knowledge acquired from fundamental courses such as “Materials Science and Engineering” and “Mechanics” which are mandatory in the Production Technology and Logistics (PTL) track of Industrial Engineering and Management (IEM) Bachelor programme.

The course unit serves as a bridge between the prerequisite courses mentioned above and subsequent courses such as “Computer Aided Design & Manufacturing” and “Design and Construction for IEM” while it also prepares students interested in conducting their Bachelor’s dissertation research on materials processing, mechanical design and engineering-related topics that are of special interest to the Advanced Production Engineering (APE) research group.

WBIE051-05.title: Industrial Biotechnology (for IEM)
WBIE051-05.priorKnowledge: The course unit assumes prior knowledge acquired from Materials and Molecules from the Bachelor IEM degree programme.

WBIE057-05.title: Mechanical Craftsmanship
WBIE057-05.priorKnowledge: The course unit assumes prior knowledge acquired from the courses WBIE011-05 Mechatronics, WBIE014-05 Production Planning and Quality Control, WBIE033-05 Computer Aided Design and Manufacturing, WBIE024-05 Mechanics for IEM, WBIE012-05 Organizational Behaviour and Group Dynamics of the Bachelor IEM (PTL track) program.

WBIE058-05.title: Applied Transport Phenomena for Sustainable Processes
WBIE058-05.priorKnowledge:
The course unit assumes prior knowledge acquired from Calculus 1 and 2, Linear Algebra, Fluid Dynamics/Physical Transport Phenomena, and Technical Thermodynamics from the Bachelor’s programmes in Industrial Engineering and Management. 
Moreover, basic programming skills are required in order to write the computer codes which are part of the reports to be presented.

WBIE061-05.title: Physical Transport Phenomena
WBIE061-05.priorKnowledge: The course unit assumes no prior knowledge acquired from previous course units but does require a solid understanding an ability to apply the Physics and Mathematics (Wiskunde B) at a level as defined by the Dutch VWO end terms.

WBIE901-20.title: Integration Project IEM
WBIE901-20.priorKnowledge:
• Successful completion of all first year BSc IEM courses.
• Successful completion of Design of Complex Systems (WBIE059-10) or Research and Design Methodology (WBIE015-05).  
• Registration of at least 140 ECTS in Progress of the study programme IEM.
• The Bachelor study programme has to be submitted to the Board of Examiners for approval.

If you do not yet fulfill these requirements, you will first  be placed on a waiting list for the course. When you do fulfill the requirements, you will be fully enrolled. If your study programme is different from the regular study programme, contact the academic advisor for enrolment in the course.

WBPH071-05.title: Materials Science and Engineering
WBPH071-05.priorKnowledge: The course unit assumes prior knowledge and skills from the following course units/degree programmes: Basic chemistry, physics and mathematics on high-school (VWO) level.

progression.schedule: The dated scheme confirms twelve year-one courses; five common year-two courses in autumn and six PTL courses in spring; and Design and Construction, Mechanical Craftsmanship and the 20 EC project in year-three spring. The 30 EC minor in year-three autumn takes the completed ordinary path to 150 EC before project entry.
progression.preparation: No compulsory examination sequence is stated in Appendices III and IV. Calculus 1 precedes Linear Algebra, and Calculus 2 follows both; these support signals and mechanics. Signals precedes Control Engineering and Complex Networks. Supply Chain prepares Production Planning. The course descriptions identify expected prior knowledge. Production Techniques uses materials and mechanics foundations. Its mention of Materials Science and Engineering as mandatory is inconsistent with Appendix IV, where it is a minor choice. Mechanics and Production Techniques share block 2a and the catalogue gives assumed knowledge, with no formal prerequisite group. The appendix controls. Mechanical Craftsmanship expects Mechatronics, which is available in the optional minor during year-three autumn. Neither expectation is a formal condition that changes the required credit grid.
progression.project: The TER requires 140 completed IEM EC including the first year and Design of Complex Systems or Research and Design Methodology. The Ocasys listing also requires submission of the study programme to the Board. An initial group methods assignment precedes the individually developed and defended research and design plan, design investigation and written thesis.
progression.minor: 30 EC in semester 1 of year 3. Eligible deepening courses, opposite-specialisation courses where eligible, approved faculty or university minors and Board-approved personal packages are allowed. Neither Mechatronics nor any other specific minor unit is treated as universally compulsory.
